definition: A grammar checker, in computing terms, is a program, or part of a program, that attempts to verify written text for grammatical correctness.
details: Grammar checkers are most often implemented as a feature of a larger program, such as a word processor, but are also available as a stand-alone application that can be activated from within programs that work with editable text. The implementation of a grammar checker makes use of natural language processing.

explainer.lead: A grammar checker is software that examines writing and attempts to determine whether it is grammatically correct. It can help people review text inside a word processor or through a separate application.

tiers.eli5: A grammar checker is like a helper who reads your writing and looks for grammar problems. It can be built into the program where you write, or it can be a separate helper you open when needed.
tiers.practitioner: Grammar checking is commonly integrated into word processors, though standalone applications can also be activated from programs that handle editable text. Its implementation uses natural language processing, and its role is to attempt grammatical verification rather than guarantee a correct assessment.
tiers.paperLevel: Given written text T, a grammar checker is a program or program component G that attempts to verify whether T is grammatically correct. Its implementation uses natural language processing; the attempt at verification does not imply that every assessment is correct.

explainer.example: Before sending a short report, a writer runs the grammar checker in a word processor. The checker processes the report's sentences and attempts to verify their grammatical correctness.

usedIn.name: Word processors
usedIn.detail: Grammar checking is most often included as a feature of a larger word-processing program.

usedIn.name: Standalone grammar-checking applications
usedIn.detail: A separate application can check text without being part of a word processor.

usedIn.name: Programs with editable text
usedIn.detail: A standalone grammar checker can be activated from within these programs.

explainer.intuition: The basic idea is to let software inspect written text for grammatical correctness. Instead of being only a separate writing tool, it often sits inside the program where the text is created.
howItWorks: The checker receives written text to examine.
It processes the text using natural language processing.
It attempts to verify the text's grammatical correctness.
The feature runs within a word processor or as an activatable standalone application.
explainer.whyItMatters: Grammar checkers bring automated grammatical review into everyday writing software. Their availability both inside word processors and as standalone applications makes them usable in different text-editing settings.
misconceptions: A grammar checker does not have to be a standalone application; it is often part of a word processor.
It attempts to verify grammatical correctness, which is not a promise of perfect verification.
